items.stem: A component has 6 V across it and 2 A flowing through it. What is its resistance?

options.rationale: Correct: R = V/I = 6 V / 2 A = 3 ohms.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about a simple SERIES circuit are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The current is the same at every point in the circuit
options.rationale: Correct: series current is the same throughout.

options.text: The total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances
Each component gets the full supply voltage
options.rationale: In series the voltage is shared between components.

options.text: Removing one component leaves the others working
options.rationale: A break in series stops all current.

items.explanation: Correct: series current is the same throughout.

items.stem: Why must you never use a mains wall socket for a classroom electricity experiment?

options.text: Mains voltage is high enough to cause serious or fatal electric shock
options.rationale: Correct: mains electricity is dangerous; only low-voltage cells should be used.

options.text: Mains electricity does not obey Ohm's law
options.rationale: Ohm's law still applies; the reason is the danger of high voltage.

options.text: Sockets do not provide enough current
options.rationale: The issue is danger, not lack of current.

options.text: Batteries give a higher voltage than mains
options.rationale: Classroom cells are far lower voltage than mains.

items.explanation: Correct: mains electricity is dangerous; only low-voltage cells should be used.
